name: Territorial nationalism
summary: Territorial nationalism holds that everyone living in a given territory forms one nation with a shared identity, whatever their ethnic, linguistic or religious differences. It grounds membership in birthplace, citizenship and allegiance, wants legal equality, and a shared public culture, and applies both to sovereign states and to sub-sovereign regions (regional nationalism). It is largely silent on economics and moral questions.
scope: The civic-territorial strand as described in Wikipedia's article, Smith's territorial model and Renan's consent-based theory: state-level and regional territorial nationalism, in Western Europe and post-independence states. Excludes ethnic nationalism and irredentist ethno-territorial variants, which the sources treat as its opposite or distortion.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology works through sovereign states or sub-sovereign regions, so a stateless society is incompatible with it.

decide-locally.rationale: Regional territorial nationalism wants local power while state territorial nationalism wants a unified national polity, so adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: It insists that religion is not a criterion of the nation and cites Islam's universalism as a rival to it, implying no privileged public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Territorial nationalism is silent here and its adherents range widely; the sources discuss legal equality of citizens but not remedial programmes.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: It seeks a shared mass public culture of common values and traditions for all inhabitants of the territory.

revolution-justified.rationale: The French Revolution is cited as a territorial nationalist uprising, but modern civic strands work through constitutions; adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism sometimes accompanies it but the territorial definition does not require it.

democracy-best.rationale: Civic-territorial nationalism is linked to constitutional and democratic government and to the people's will, though state nationalism can be illiberal.

right-to-secede.rationale: Regional territorial nationalists claim self-rule or independence while state territorial nationalists defend the existing territory, so the ideology is genuinely split.

natural-rulers.rationale: It stresses equal citizenship and legal equality of all inhabitants, which excludes born rulers.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is not a criterion of the nation, and Renan rejects religion as its basis, so religion cannot define the state community.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A national identity open to people of every religion cannot rest on scripture-based law; the article contrasts it with Islamic universality.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining claim is that all inhabitants of a territory share a national identity regardless of ethnic, linguistic or religious differences.

civilizational-union.rationale: The ideology ties the nation to a particular territory and contrasts itself with larger religious solidarities such as Islamic universality.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Communist regimes suppressed territorial 'bourgeois nationalism', and the idea of one national community cuts against class dictatorship.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Regional and minority territorial nationalism claim collective rights for territorial communities, though civic strands stress individual rights.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Renan holds a nation has no interest in annexing a country against its will, and ethnic-conquest claims are the ethnic variant.

national-self-determination.rationale: The sources tie the nation to a sovereign state or a self-governing territorial region; Renan wants disputed populations consulted.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources discuss national identity, not epistemology, so adherents of any outlook can hold the doctrine.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine unites all classes in a territorial national community.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legal equality of all inhabitants regardless of ethnicity is essential to it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Eastern Bloc communists branded it bourgeois, but it itself treats the state as the common community.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Western territorial nations rest on birthplace, and the article describes a shared public culture, yet it also stresses retained differences and choice; adherents split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Its core idea that anyone in the territory can belong rules out replacement narratives.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The doctrine rejects race and ethnicity as bases of belonging.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Legal equality of all inhabitants is described as essential, and liberal civic nationalism upholds equality and rights. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Renan makes consent, a daily plebiscite, the basis of the nation, and civic nationalism follows it.

population-transfer.rationale: The Wikipedia article ties territorial nationalism to expulsion and ethnic cleansing as well as to the inclusive civic model the scope follows, so opposition to expelling minorities is a contested lean.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The doctrine stresses shared effort and common will.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources on civic nationalism do not address banning parties; liberal and state-centred strands differ.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: It holds that a shared territorial identity unites diverse ethnic, linguistic and religious groups.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Allegiance may be adopted, so citizenship should be open.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command of the armed forces is a constitutional matter the doctrine leaves open.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion cannot define the nation; Renan rejects it as basis.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romantic ruralism belongs to other nationalisms; territorial nationalism defines the nation by territory and citizenship.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irredentism is described as a source of ethnic conflict, but self-determination by the populations is central; both camps exist.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: It tolerates all cultures within the territory.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Western territorial nationalism bases national identity on birthplace more than ethnicity, favouring birth on the soil.

minority-language-support.rationale: It accepts linguistic differences among inhabitants and regional territorial nationalism often demands them.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Territorial nationalists in post-colonial states have split on whether independence required economic transformation.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Renan rejects 'historical right' to territory in favour of inhabitants' will.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Renan says a province is its inhabitants and a nation never gains by annexing against its will.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: State territorial nationalism defends territorial integrity while regional types seek autonomy; adherents split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Regional territorial nationalists sometimes seek this, but the sources give no general view.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Legal equality and constitutional citizenship exclude a ruler above the law.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Renan says nationality is not language or race, but the article says territorial nationalism sometimes leads to irredentism, as with Greater Morocco and Greater Mauritania, so rejection of co-ethnic claims is contested.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is no national criterion and civic nationalism holds tolerance.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union of peoples by ancestry is the ethnic model; Renan rejects race and language.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Allegiance is owed to the country of birth or adoption with full legal equality.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Legal equality of all inhabitants is essential.

patriotic-education.rationale: It seeks a mass public culture of shared values and traditions.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Whether parliament is supreme over a monarch is a constitutional matter the doctrine leaves open.

native-born-offices.rationale: Allegiance may be adopted, so adopted citizens are equal.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The article ties irredentism to territorial nationalism while Renan rejects claims from historical right, so adherents are split on reclaiming lost land.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The doctrine does not rank civilizations; post-independence territorial nationalists differ on adopting Western institutions.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism sometimes accompanies the doctrine, but it does not require blocking foreign purchases.

single-official-language.rationale: It accommodates linguistic differences among inhabitants; Renan says language does not define a nation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The sources are silent on NGO funding rules; civic liberals and state nationalists would differ.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The civic model includes all inhabitants as members, leaving no room for a conspiring minority.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion is explicitly not a criterion; Renan and the article hold that nationality is independent of religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional territorial nationalists may want fiscal autonomy while state ones favour national sharing.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is part of ethnolinguistic nationalism, while this type does not define nation by language.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settling a majority in minority regions links to ethnic claims on land that the inclusive model rejects.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Renan rejects so-called historical right in favour of inhabitants' consent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religion is not a criterion of the nation and tolerance is a civic value.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The article contrasts territorial nationalism with Islamic universality.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Territorial nationalism sets national territory ahead of religious universality.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine is a theory of national membership, not a claim about the left-right axis.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority rests on the will of the people in the nation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Neutrality is a foreign-policy choice the doctrine does not dictate.

property-franchise.rationale: Legal equality of inhabitants is essential to it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Legal equality and the rejection of ethnic criteria make race-limited franchise incompatible with it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religion is no national criterion, making such restrictions contrary to an inclusive model.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inclusive membership of all inhabitants contradicts it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: It does not make religion a criterion either way and Eastern Bloc nationalisms were suppressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not part of its civic form.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereignty over territory is central, but the sources do not treat foreign bases, so adherents split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Renan stresses shared memory and forgetting, a modern daily act of will.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring martyrs belongs to sacralising nationalisms; the sources give no such feature for the territorial type.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A metaphysical view of politics is not part of this civic, consent-based nationalism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Allegiance is to the country of birth or adoption, not a distant homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: The doctrine is statist or regional-political.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic primacy contradicts equal citizenship.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Territorial nationalists use existing territorial units, not units of one people.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The sources discuss regional nationalism but not municipal confederation.

person-over-state.rationale: The sources define the nation by citizenship but do not state a personalist philosophy.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Renan calls the nation a spiritual principle, but this is about the nation, not human nature generally.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Ethnicity and race are not criteria of belonging; a single shared national identity is the core.

racial-pride.rationale: Race does not ground the nation; Renan rejects slavery to race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The doctrine holds that inhabitants share one nation whatever their language, and Renan rejects language as the criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Single civic citizenship rather than communal voting.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Partition fears appear in some states, but the sources do not make this a doctrinal belief.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomatic secrecy is not covered, and adherents differ.

sacred-nation.rationale: Renan's nation is a will, a daily plebiscite, not a sacred being.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional territorial nationalists often say so; state-level ones do not.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear policy is not part of the doctrine, and territorial states have differed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Territorial nationalists in post-colonial states have differed on role of chiefs; the sources are silent.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources link civic nationalism to democracy but give no definition of democracy.

women-suffrage.rationale: Legal equality is essential to the doctrine.

race-social-construct.rationale: It rejects race as basis; Renan says race does not bind.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Regional territorial nationalism is a recognised form of the doctrine; Smith/Kymlicka note territorial autonomy for minorities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Renan says a province is its inhabitants and disputed populations should be consulted.

close-ties-china.rationale: Territorial nationalism is silent on foreign alignment, and states of this kind choose differently.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Membership rests on territory and citizenship, not ethnicity, and irredentist support for kin abroad is treated as its distortion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Territorial nationalism does not address culture's relation to technology, and adherents differ.

multipolar-world.rationale: Territorial nationalism concerns the state's population, not world order; adherents differ.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Territorial nationalism unites all inhabitants but the sources do not tie that to a working-class politics, and adherents are split.

missingStatements.text: All inhabitants of a country's territory, whatever their ethnicity, language or religion, belong to one nation.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of the ideology.

missingStatements.text: The inhabitants of a disputed territory should decide which country it belongs to.
missingStatements.rationale: Renan says a province is its inhabitants and disputed populations should be consulted.

notes: Regional (sub-state) territorial nationalism and state-level territorial nationalism answer differently on secession and decentralisation, so those are marked as split. Most economic and moral statements are outside the ideology.
